This Code constitutes a codification of the general and permanent ordinances of Tattnall County, Georgia.
Source materials used in the preparation of the Code were the ordinances as adopted by the Tattnall County Board of Commissioners through September 9, 2013. The source of each section is included in the history note appearing in parentheses at the end thereof. The absence of such a note indicates that the section is new and was adopted for the first time with the adoption of the Code. By use of the comparative tables appearing in the back of this Code, the reader can locate any ordinance included herein.
The chapters of the Code have been conveniently arranged in alphabetical order, and the various sections within each chapter have been catchlined to facilitate usage. Notes which tie related sections of the Code together and which refer to relevant state law have been included. A table listing the state law citations and setting forth their location within the Code is included at the back of this Code.
Chapter and Section Numbering System
The chapter and section numbering system used in this Code is the same system used in many state and local government codes. Each section number consists of two parts separated by a dash. The figure before the dash refers to the chapter number, and the figure after the dash refers to the position of the section within the chapter. Thus, the second section of chapter 1 is numbered 1-2, and the first section of chapter 6 is 6-1. Under this system, each section is identified with its chapter, and at the same time new sections can be inserted in their proper place by using the decimal system for amendments. For example, if new material consisting of one section that would logically come between sections 6-1 and 6-2 is desired to be added, such new section would be numbered 6-1.5. New articles and new divisions may be included in the same way or, in the case of articles, may be placed at the end of the chapter embracing the subject, and, in the case of divisions, may be placed at the end of the article embracing the subject. The next successive number shall be assigned to the new article or division. New chapters may be included by using one of the reserved chapter numbers. Care should be taken that the alphabetical arrangement of chapters is maintained when including new chapters.
Page Numbering System
The page numbering system used in this Code is a prefix system. The letters to the left of the colon are an abbreviation which represents a certain portion of the volume. The number to the right of the colon represents the number of the page in that portion. In the case of a chapter of the Code, the number to the left of the colon indicates the number of the chapter. In the case of an appendix to the Code, the letter immediately to the left of the colon indicates the letter of the appendix. Indexes
The indexes have been prepared with the greatest of care. Each particular item has been placed under several headings, some of which are couched in lay phraseology, others in legal terminology, and still others in language generally used by local government officials and employees. There are numerous cross references within the indexes themselves which stand as guideposts to direct the user to the particular item in which the user is interested.
Looseleaf Supplements
A special feature of this publication is the looseleaf system of binding and supplemental servicing of the publication. With this system, the publication will be kept up to date. Subsequent amendatory legislation will be properly edited, and the affected page or pages will be reprinted. These new pages will be distributed to holders of copies of the publication, with instructions for the manner of inserting the new pages and deleting the obsolete pages.
Keeping this publication up to date at all times will depend largely upon the holder of the publication. As revised pages are received, it will then become the responsibility of the holder to have the amendments inserted according to the attached instructions. It is strongly recommended by the publisher that all such amendments be inserted immediately upon receipt to avoid misplacing them and, in addition, that all deleted pages be saved and filed for historical reference purposes.

This publication was under the direct supervision of Jim Jenkins, Senior Code Attorney, and Nicole C. Fluitt, Editor, of the Municipal Code Corporation, Tallahassee, Florida. Credit is gratefully given to the other members of the publisher's staff for their sincere interest and able assistance throughout the project.

It is hoped that their efforts and those of the publisher have resulted in a Code of Ordinances which will make the active law of Tattnall County readily accessible to all citizens and which will be a valuable tool in the day-to-day administration of the county's affairs.

ORDINANCE NO. 03-26-15
AN ORDINANCE ADOPTING AND ENACTING A NEW CODE FOR THE CODE OF TATTNALL COUNTY, GEORGIA; PROVIDING FOR THE REPEAL OF CERTAIN ORDINANCES NOT INCLUDED THEREIN; PROVIDING A PENALTY FOR THE VIOLATION THEREOF; PROVIDING FOR THE MANNER OF AMENDING SUCH CODE; AND PROVIDING WHEN SUCH CODE AND THIS ORDINANCE SHALL BECOME EFFECTIVE.
BE IT ORDAINED BY THE:
Section 1. The Code entitled "The Code of Tattnall County, Georgia," published by Municipal Code Corporation, consisting of chapters 1 through 70, each inclusive, is adopted.
Section 2. All ordinances of a general and permanent nature enacted on or before September 9, 2013, and not included in the Code or recognized and continued in force by reference therein, are repealed.
Section 3. The repeal provided for in section 2 hereof shall not be construed to revive any ordinance or part thereof that has been repealed by a subsequent ordinance that is repealed by this ordinance.
Section 4. Unless another penalty is expressly provided, every person convicted of a violation of any provision of the Code or any ordinance, rule or regulation adopted or issued in pursuance thereof shall be punished by a fine not to exceed $1,000.00 and imprisonment in the county jail and work and labor on the streets or public works of the county, whether within or without the corporate limits, not to exceed one year, or both a fine and sentence of imprisonment and labor; and all sentences may be in the alternative and fines may be imposed with the alternative of sentence to imprisonment and labor if the fines are not paid. Each act of violation and each day upon which any such violation shall continue or occur shall constitute a separate offense. The penalty provided by this section, unless another penalty is expressly provided, shall apply to the amendment of any Code section, whether or not such penalty is reenacted in the amendatory ordinance. In addition to the penalty prescribed above, the County may pursue other remedies such as abatement of nuisances, injunctive relief and revocation of licenses or permits.
Section 5. Additions or amendments to the Code when passed in such form as to indicate the intention of the County to make the same a part of the Code shall be deemed to be incorporated in the Code, so that reference to the Code includes the additions and amendments.
Section 6. Ordinances adopted after September 9, 2013, that amend or refer to ordinances that have been codified in the Code shall be construed as if they amend or refer to like provisions of the Code.
Section 7. This ordinance shall become effective March 26, 2015.
Passed and adopted by the Board of County Commissioners this 26th day of March 2015.

(a) Board of commissioners. A Board of Commissioners of Tattnall County is created to consist of six members, one of whom shall be chairman and each of whom shall be elected to office as provided in this section. Each commissioner shall be a qualified voter and a resident of Tattnall County for at least one year and shall have resided in the district from which such member is elected for a period of not less than six months prior to the time that such member qualifies for election. Each commissioner shall serve a term of four years and shall be eligible to succeed in office.
(b) Method of election.
(1) The chairman of the board shall be elected by a majority vote of the qualified voters of the entire county pursuant to Chapter 2 of Title 21 of the O.C.G.A., the 'Georgia Election Code,' as amended. The chairman shall be a resident and qualified voter of Tattnall County and shall have resided in the county for a period not less than one year prior to the time that such person qualifies for election.
(2) The other five commissioners shall qualify for election in the road district in which such member resides and shall be elected by a majority vote of the qualified voters of such road district as the districts are set out in section 1B. Only residents of a district may vote in the primary and general elections for candidates for commissioners from that district.
(c) (1) The term of office of the chairperson of the commission elected in the November general election in 2000, who took office on January 1, 2001, shall end December 31, 2004. A successor shall be elected in the state-wide general election in 2004 and shall take office on January 1, 2005.
(2) The provisions of paragraphs (3) and (4) of this subsection are intended to implement the consent order entered in Windgate, et al. v. Tattnall County, Georgia v. Williams, et al., Civil Action CV600-070, ___ Fed. Supp. ___ (S. D. Ga.) 2000.
(3) A special election shall be held at the time of and in conjunction with the general primary election in July, 2002, to elect the five members of the board of commissioners from the road districts described in section 1B and enacted at the same time as this section. The term of office of the members of the commission elected in the November general election in 2001, who took office on January 1, 2002, shall end when their successors are elected in the special election provided for in this paragraph and qualified.
(4) The terms of office of the members of the board of commissioners elected in July, 2002, in accordance with paragraph (2) of this subsection shall end December 31, 2004. Their successors shall be nominated and elected in the state-wide general election in 2004 and shall take office on January 1, 2005.
(5) Thereafter, successors to the chairperson and members of the board of commissioners whose terms are to expire shall be elected at the time of the state-wide general election immediately preceding the expiration of such terms, shall take office the first day of January immediately following that election, and shall serve for terms of office of four years each. The chairperson and members of the board shall serve for the terms of office specified in this subsection and until their respective successors are elected and qualified.
(d) Vacancies. In the event a vacancy occurs on the board of commissioners for any reason other than the expiration of the term of office, the vacancy shall be filled in accordance with the provisions of Code Section 36-5-21 of the O.C.G.A., Chapter 2 of Title 21 of the O.C.G.A., the 'Georgia Election Code,' and the residency requirements set out in this Act. In the event a member moves such member's residence from the district such member represents, a vacancy shall exist from such district and shall be filled in the same manner as other vacancies are filled.
(e) Oath of office. All commissioners, before entering upon their duties as such, shall take an oath on the faithful and diligent performance of their duties as commissioners before the judge of the Probate Court of Tattnall County.
(f) Bond. Before any commissioner shall qualify and assume any duties of office, such member shall give bond, approved by the probate judge, in the following amounts and payable to the probate judge of Tattnall County, Georgia, for the faithful performance of all duties of commissioners:
(1) Chairman of county commissioners $25,000.00
(2) Commissioners 10,000.00
All bonds shall be issued by some solvent surety company authorized to do business in the State of Georgia, and the premiums for such bonds shall be paid by the county.
(g) Officers. At the first meeting of the board held during January of each year, or at such other times as vacancies in office may necessitate, the board shall elect such officers, other than the chairman, as they deem necessary to serve for the ensuing calendar year. The chairman shall be entitled to vote only in cases of a tie. The board is authorized to employ an administrative assistant to the board who shall receive such compensation as the board shall fix, serve at the pleasure of the board, and discharge such duties and responsibilities as shall be assigned and delegated to such administrative assistant by the board.
(h) Meetings; quorum; voting. The board shall hold at least one session on the first Monday in each month in the courthouse, where the clerk of said board shall keep a regular office. At the request of a majority of the board, the chairman may, at any time, call an extra session. Written notice of such extra sessions shall be served on each member unless members in attendance waive such notice. The board shall have the right to adjourn from day to day until they finish their business. No fewer than four members of said board shall constitute a quorum for the transaction of business on any subject matter, and all questions coming before the board shall be determined by a majority vote of those present and voting. The chairman shall be eligible to vote only in the case of a tie vote.
(i) Salaries and expenses. Commissioners shall receive as compensation for their services as commissioners the sum of $428.83 per month. The chairperson shall receive as compensation for his or her services the sum of $818.92. In addition to the monthly salaries provided in this subsection, each commissioner shall receive an expense supplement in the sum of $400.00 per month and the chairperson shall receive an expense supplement in the sum of $500.00 per month. The expense supplement is an addition to all salaries and shall cover the costs of expenses incurred by said commissioners during the performance of their duties of office. Upon approval by a majority vote of the board of commissioners, the chairperson shall also be furnished a motor vehicle for use in carrying out the duties of his or her office. The cost of such motor vehicle and the reasonable expenses of operating and maintaining such motor vehicle shall be paid from county funds. The chairperson may allow any member of the board of commissioners to use such motor vehicle in carrying out the duties of such member's office. No other form of compensation or benefit, either directly or indirectly, shall be received by a commissioner, including the chairperson, for the performance of his or her official duties as a county commissioner of Tattnall County.
(j) Duties. It shall be the duty of the commissioners, among other things, to keep up the roadways within the county; to provide for fair, equitable, and adequate distribution of maintenance and repair of roadways among the districts, both those existing now and those to exist in the future; to provide for the public welfare of the citizens of the county according to their requirements, from time to time; to keep accurate and permanent records of county business and affairs; to keep the courthouse and all county buildings, offices, and polling places in good repair; to provide for public health services as are authorized by law and to enforce existing health codes; to keep the county free of litter, trash, garbage, and all other forms of environmental pollution; to fairly and equitably levy and collect such taxes and assessments as are authorized by law; to fairly and equitably allocate the expenditure of taxes collected so that public needs shall be fairly and equitably addressed; to assist, from time to time, municipal governments within the county in providing for essential public services; to abide by all laws and ordinances respecting the operation of county government and the performance of commissioners' duties and to exercise only those powers granted in this subsection and by the Constitution and laws of the State of Georgia.
(1985 Ga. Laws (Act No. 432), page 4624, § 1; 1990 Ga. Laws (Act No. 874), page 4207, § 1; 2002 Ga. Laws (Act No. 452), page 3916, § 1; 2002 Ga. Laws (Act No. 612), page 4730, § 1)

(a) County clerk and assistant clerks. The commissioners shall employ a full-time county clerk and such assistant clerks as needs require. The commissioners shall fix their salaries and duties as the business affairs of the county require. It shall be the duty of the clerk to keep the business records of the county as well as the official minutes and records of all resolutions and ordinances; to manage the day-to-day business affairs of the commissioner's office; to assist the chairman and any commissioner in any county matter; and to perform such other duties as this Act or the laws of the State of Georgia require. It shall be the duty of the county clerk to maintain the business records of the county in an accurate, current, and permanent state. Neither the county clerk nor any assistant clerk shall be a member of the board of commissioners.
(b) County records. The county clerk shall maintain separate and distinct record books for the keeping of official minutes, resolutions and ordinances, county right-of-way records, and the county road index. The county clerk shall make all county records available for public inspection upon request by any resident of the county; provided, however, that any such inspection shall be permitted at such times and under such circumstances as shall not interfere with the normal day-to-day operation of the county commissioner's office.
(1985 Ga. Laws (Act No. 432), page 4624, § 1)

The board shall be composed of three members, each of whom shall be an elector and resident of Tattnall County, and shall be appointed in the following manner:
(1) One member shall be appointed by the chairperson of the Tattnall County executive committee of the political party whose candidate for Governor at the last preceding general election received the largest number of votes within the county. One member shall be appointed by the chairperson of the Tattnall County executive committee of the political party whose candidate for Governor at such election received the next largest number of such votes. Board of commissioners, board of county commissioners, commissioner, board, or governing authority. The term "board of commissioners," "board of county commissioners," "commissioner," "board," or "governing authority" means the board of county commissioners of Tattnall County, Georgia.

Computation of time. Except as otherwise provided by time period computations specifically applying to other laws, when a period of time measured in days, weeks, months, years or other measurements of time except hours is prescribed for the exercise of any privilege or the discharge of any duty, the first day shall not be counted but the last day shall be counted; and, if the last day falls on Saturday or Sunday, the party having such privilege or duty shall have through the following Monday to exercise the privilege or to discharge the duty. When the last day prescribed for such action falls on a public and legal holiday as set forth in O.C.G.A. § 1-4-1, the party having the privilege or duty shall have through the next business day to exercise the privilege or to discharge the duty. When the period of time prescribed is less than seven days, intermediate Saturdays, Sundays and legal holidays shall be excluded in the computation.
Conjunctions. In a provision involving two or more items, conditions, provisions or events, which items, conditions, provisions or events are connected by the conjunction "and," "or" or "either … or," the conjunction shall be interpreted as follows, except that in appropriate cases the terms "or" and "and" are interchangeable:
(1) "And" indicates that all the connected terms, conditions, provisions or events apply.
(2) "Or" indicates that the connected terms, conditions, provisions or events apply singly or in any combination.
(3) "Either … or" indicates that the connected terms, conditions, provisions or events apply singly but not in combination.
County. The term "county" or "the county" means the County of Tattnall, State of Georgia.
Day. The term "day" means a calendar day of 24 hours.
Delegation of authority. Whenever a provision appears requiring the head of a department of the county to do some act or make certain inspections, it is to be construed to authorize the head of the department to designate, delegate and authorize subordinates to perform the required act or make the required inspection unless the terms of the provision or section designate otherwise.
Gender. Terms importing the masculine gender shall include the feminine and neuter.
Interpretation. In the interpretation and application of any provision of this Code, it shall be held to be the minimum requirements adopted for the promotion of the public health, safety, comfort, convenience and general welfare. Where any provision of the Code imposes greater restrictions upon the subject matter than the general provision imposed by the Code, the provision imposing the greater restriction or regulation shall be deemed to be controlling.
Joint authority. All terms giving joint authority to three or more persons or officers shall be construed as giving such authority to a majority of such persons or officers, except when such words are used to grant authority to the chairperson and board of county commissioners.
Keeper and proprietor. The terms "keeper" and "proprietor" mean and include persons, firms, associations, corporations, receivers, trustees, personal representatives, clubs and partnerships, whether acting by themselves or through a servant, agent or employee.
Month. The term "month" means a calendar month.
Names of officers and departments. The name or title of any officer or department shall be read as though the words "of Tattnall County" were added thereto.
Nontechnical and technical words. Number. Terms used in the singular include the plural and the plural includes the singular number.
Oath. The term "oath" shall be construed to include an affirmation in all cases in which, by law, an affirmation may be substituted for an oath, and in such cases the terms "swear" and "sworn" shall be equivalent to the terms "affirm" and "affirmed."

Overlapping provisions. Where any provision of this Code imposes greater restrictions upon the subject matter than any general provisions imposed by this Code, the provision imposing the greater restriction or regulation shall be applicable.

Person. The term "person" includes a corporation, firm, partnership, association, organization and any other group acting as a unit, as well as an individual.

Preceding, following. The terms "preceding" and "following" mean next before and next after, respectively.
Premises. Whenever the term "premises" is used, it shall mean place or places.

Year. The term "year" means a calendar year.

(a) Policy. In compliance with the Americans with Disabilities Act, 42 U.S.C. 12101 et seq., 1990, and 28 CFR 35.107(B) the county desires to establish a policy for providing disabled individuals a local grievance procedure for resolution of complaints lodged under the Act. It is the board's stated intention that this policy is intended to assist disabled individuals by providing access to the programs, services and facilities of county government.
(b) Administration. The board as an official portion of this policy and procedure has established several administrative positions with certain responsibilities as follows:
(1) ADA coordinator. The county manager shall serve, or appoint a designee to serve, as ADA coordinator until his successor is appointed. It shall be the duty and responsibility of this individual to maintain all files and records of the county relating to records, grievances and audits for the prescribed period pursuant to the Americans with Disabilities Act. In addition, the coordinator shall be responsible for ensuring that the provision of this grievance policy are implemented and conducted fairly under the terms of the Americans with Disabilities Act and 28 CFR 35.107, and as these may be amended from time to time. The coordinator's name shall be posted on the notices as required by the Act.
(2) ADA department representative. Each county department shall designate an individual within the department to serve as ADA representative whose departmental individual charged with providing responses and coordination of information and the processing of grievances.
(3) ADA committee panel. The county manager is hereby authorized to select, in coordination with the county ADA coordinator, a panel of not less than two people to hear appeals or grievances filed pursuant to this policy. It shall be the duty of the panel to render timely decisions and to utilize its best efforts to resolve any disputes presented by the grievance regarding matters under the Americans with Disabilities ACT and 28 CFR 35.107, and as these may be amended from time to time.
(c) Procedure for filing and considering a grievance.
(1) Any individual desiring to file a grievance shall complete the ADA grievance form as established by the county. The completed form should be submitted to the department ADA representative no later than five working days after the grievant becomes aware of the alleged violation or questioned activity.
(2) Thereafter, the department's ADA representative shall investigate and review the complaint and meet with the grievant within three working days when possible. (a) No license issued hereunder shall be suspended, revoked or placed on probation except for due cause as herein defined, and after a hearing before the board of commissioners following written notice to the holder of such license of the time, place and purpose of such hearing addressed to licensee at the last address which licensee provided to the county or to the address of the premises and a statement of the charge upon which such hearing shall be held, except as hereinafter provided. (c) In all hearings pursuant to this section, the following procedures shall prevail, and the proceeding shall be as informal as compatible with justice:
(1) The chairman of the board of commissioners shall read or cause to be read the charges and specifications against the licensee. He shall then read or cause to be read any response filed by the licensee.
(2) The board of commissioners shall hear the evidence upon the charges and specifications as filed against the licensee and shall not consider any additional evidence beyond the scope of the charge, and may exclude evidence which is purely cumulative.
(3) The order of proof shall be as follows: The county representative shall present his evidence in support of the charges; the licensee shall then present his evidence. Evidence of each party may be supported by submission of pertinent documents. Each party shall be allowed to present pertinent rebuttal evidence.
(4) The licensee and county may be represented by counsel, and may present, examine and cross-examine witnesses. Additionally, the board of commissioners may interrogate all parties and witnesses to obtain necessary information.

As accusation by a law enforcement officer shall be deemed due and sufficient cause for suspension. A license shall not be revoked except upon action by the board of commissioners.

Except as otherwise set forth in this chapter and except where the context clearly indicates a different meaning, the following words, terms and phrases, when used in this chapter, shall have the meanings ascribed to them in this section:
Alcohol means ethyl alcohol, hydrated oxide of ethyl, or spirits of wine, from whatever source or by whatever process produced.
Alcoholic beverage means and includes all alcohol, distilled spirits, beer, malt beverage, wine or fortified wine.
Applicant means the person or entity applying for any license authorized by this chapter.
Application means the written form approved and/or generated by the governing authority which must be completed and executed by any applicant for any license authorized by this chapter.
Beer or malt beverage means any alcoholic beverage obtained by the fermentation of any infusion or decoction of barley, malt, hops, or any other product, or any combination of such products in water, containing not more than six percent alcohol by volume, and including ale, porter, brown, stout, lager beer, small beer, and strong beer. The term "malt beverage" does not include sake, known as Japanese rice wine.
Brown bag establishment means any restaurant, music hall, theater, or other establishment providing food or entertainment in the normal course of business, and in which the owners or their agents knowingly allow patrons to bring in and consume the patron's own alcoholic beverages.
Church building means as a free-standing structure, originally built for use as a church, but does not mean a commercial or retail building or space that has been converted for occupancy by a church or for religious purposes.
Code means the Code of Ordinances of Tattnall County, Georgia.
County means Tattnall County, Georgia, and the land within the boundaries and territory of Tattnall County, Georgia.
Distilled spirits means any alcoholic beverage obtained by distillation or containing more than 21 percent alcohol by volume including, but not limited to, all fortified wines.
Fortified wine means any alcoholic beverage containing more than 21 percent alcohol by volume made from fruits, berries, or grapes, either by natural fermentation or by natural fermentation with brandy added. The term "fortified wine" includes, but is not limited to, brandy.
Governing authority means the board of commissioners of Tattnall County, Georgia.
Hotel means any lodge, inn, or similar establishment which offers overnight sleeping accommodations to registered guests for hire, and at which prepared meals or food are regularly served daily and consumed in one or more dining rooms, having an adequate and sanitary kitchen, such sleeping accommodations and dining rooms being conducted on the same premises. Hotels may grant franchises for the operation of a restaurant and lounge on their premises, and the holder of such franchise shall be included in this definition of a hotel. Lounges may be located separately from dining facilities in hotels provided there is a commonality of ownership of the restaurant and lounge.
License means the authorization granted by the governing authority of the county to engage in the sale of alcoholic beverages in a specified manner for a calendar year or the remaining portion of a calendar year.
Licensee means the person to whom a license is issued or, in the case of any type of partnership, limited liability company or corporation, all partners, officers, managers and directors of the partnership, limited liability company or corporation, and the use of a masculine, feminine or neutral pronoun to describe licensee will contemplate the correct licensee even if the incorrect pronoun is used.
Liter means metric measurement, currently used by the United States.
Manager means the person who supervises any operations, business, activity or location of any person licensed under this chapter.
Manufacturer means any maker, producer, or bottler of an alcoholic beverage. The word "manufacturer" also means:
(1) In the case of distilled spirits, any person engaged in distilling, rectifying, or blending any distilled spirits.
(2) In the case of malt beverages, any brewer.
Minor means any person under the age of 21 years.
Owner means any person, partner, stockholder or member owning any percentage of an activity, business or operation.
Package means a bottle, can, keg, barrel or other original consumer container.
Person means any individual, firm, partnership, cooperative, nonprofit corporation, joint venture, association, company, corporation, limited liability company, agency, syndicate, estate, trust, business trust, receiver, fiduciary, or other group or combination acting as a unit, body politic, or political subdivision, whether public, private or quasi-public.
Premises means the space or area owned, leased or controlled by the licensee and used by the licensee for the purpose of operating under the license including any public sidewalk or roadway adjacent to the premises which is used by the licensee to sell or distribute alcoholic beverages.
Public club means an establishment, other than a restaurant as defined in this chapter, having the principal purpose of offering live music, dancing, theatrical productions or comedians, and at which the consumption of alcoholic beverages on the premises only is an attendant purpose. A public club shall not be operated or conducted in conjunction with any other type of business, trade or profession and may offer and sale only those items commonly associated with such establishments.
Public place means any place that the public is invited or permitted to go or congregate.
Purchaser means any individual, partnership, corporation, limited liability company, trust or association purchasing alcoholic beverages from a licensee.
Restaurant means any public place used, maintained, advertised and held out to the public as a place where meals are actually and regularly served, without sleeping accommodations, such place being provided with adequate and sanitary kitchen, where the principal business is the sale of food, and that:
(1) Fills 75 percent of the usable square footage of its primary premises, including decks and patios which are immediately adjacent to and a part of its primary premises, with tables and chairs intended for dining,
(2) Is staffed at all times while open to the public with a sufficient number and kind of employees to prepare, cook, and serve edible food to its guests,
(3) Is open to the public at least four hours a day, serving at least one meal per day,
(4) Serves meals at least five days a week with the exception of weeks including holidays, vacations and periods of maintenance, construction or remodeling,
(5) Does not have a common table or counter area that comprises more than 25 percent of its dining area, and
(6) Derives at least 50 percent of its total annual gross sales from the sale of prepared meals and food, and in calculating annual gross sales, it shall use all of its receipts, including those of persons laboring on the premises, such as all employees, independent contractors, performers, servers and entertainers.
Retail dealer means any person who sells alcoholic beverages, either in unbroken packages or for consumption on the premises, at retail only, to consumers and not for resale.
School means any school building, school grounds, college campus, educational facility or educational building owned or run by or affiliated with a state, county, city or private or religious entity, any church school, day care, or kindergarten and to any building at such other schools in which are taught subjects commonly taught in the common schools and colleges of this state. It shall not apply to home schools.
Wholesaler or wholesale dealer means any person who sells alcoholic beverages to other wholesale dealers, to retail dealers, or to retail consumption dealers.
Wine means any alcoholic beverage containing not more than 21 percent alcohol by volume made from fruits, berries, or grapes, either by natural fermentation or by natural fermentation with brandy added. The term "wine" includes, but is not limited to, all sparkling wines, champagnes, combinations of such beverages, vermouths, special natural wines, rectified wines and like products. The term "wine" does not include cooking wine mixed with salt or other ingredients so as to render it unfit for human consumption as a beverage. A liquid shall first be deemed to be a wine at that point in the manufacturing process when it conforms to the definition of wine contained in this section.
(Ord. No. 2022-3, § I, 7-11-2022; Ord. No. 23-1, § I, 1-9-2023)

(e) Any licensee who proposes to change the location of the licensed premises within the unincorporated area of the county shall so notify the county clerk in writing at least 30 days prior to any proposed change of location. The notice of proposed change of location shall be accompanied by a survey as required by subsection (a) of this section. A licensee's business shall not change location unless the new location complies with all provisions of this chapter. The governing authority shall have the authority to approve or deny the change of location in the same manner that it may approve or deny the issuance of a new license. An investigative fee of $200.00 shall be paid by the licensee at the time that a notice of change of location is made. If a change of location is approved, with no change of ownership of the business, the license fee paid for the old location shall be applied to the new location.
(f) Any licensee who desires to change the manager or name of the licensed business or premises shall so notify the county clerk in writing at least 30 days prior to any change of manager or name, and the county clerk shall direct the issuance of a corrected license in replacement of the original license, or, in the case of a change of manager, such licensee shall ftle with the county clerk such information about the new manager as the county clerk may require. A fee of $25.00 shall be paid by the licensee at the time that such notice is given for the change of manager or name of such business or premises.
(g) Except as provided in this section, any change in the ownership or control of any licensee shall be cause to revoke any license issued under this chapter.
(Ord. No. 2022-3, § I, 7-11-2022; Ord. No. 23-1, § I, 1-9-2023)
151:
(a) No license shall be issued to any elected official of the county or any employee of the county, nor shall any such person have any whole, partial or beneficial interest in any license.
(b) No license shall be issued in connection with any premises that fails to meet:
(1) All applicable fire, life safety, building and health laws, rules and regulations under state law or the Code, and
(2) Any applicable zoning ordinances and regulations of the Code.
(c) No license shall be issued to any applicant who is delinquent in the payment of county taxes or fees, including, but not limited to property taxes, alcoholic beverage excise taxes, business license fees, occupational taxes, or any other tax or fee which is owed to the county by the applicant.
(Ord. No. 2022-3, § I, 7-11-2022; Ord. No. 23-1, § I, 1-9-2023)
152:
Where a person applies for a license in connection with any premises that is not yet in existence or completed, a license may be issued for such premises; provided that, the plans for such premises comply with this chapter and the Code. No sales shall be allowed in such premises until it has been completed in accordance with such plans, a certificate of occupancy issued, and it has been inspected by the proper state and/or county officials, including but not limited to the county manager, county administrator, county building inspector, county code enforcement officer or the county sheriff, or any of his or her deputies, to ensure compliance with this chapter and the Code.
(Ord. No. 2022-3, § I, 7-11-2022; Ord. No. 23-1, § I, 1-9-2023)
153:
(a) All licensed premises must open for business within six months after issuance of the license. Failure to do so shall serve as a ground for revocation of such license by the governing authority, unless an extension of time is granted by the county manager or administrator before the expiration of the six-month period, for good cause shown by the licensee. No refund of the license fee shall be made in the event of a revocation hereunder.
(b) Any licensee who begins operating the business or premises authorized in the license, but who thereafter ceases operation for six months within any calendar year, shall be subject to revocation of his license by the governing authority, unless an extension of time is granted by the county manager or administrator before the expiration of the six-month period, for good cause shown by the licensee. No refund of license fee shall be made in the event of a revocation hereunder.
(Ord. No. 2022-3, § I, 7-11-2022; Ord. No. 23-1, § I, 1-9-2023)
154:
(a) All licenses shall expire on December 31 of each year. A licensee who desires to renew the license shall file an application, with the requisite fees as set forth in this chapter, with the county clerk on the form provided for renewal of the license for the ensuing year. All applications for renewal will be reviewed by the county clerk. A licensee does not have a right to automatic renewal and must be compliant with this chapter when applying for the renewal of his or her license. Applications for renewal must be filed on or before November 30 of each year; otherwise, a penalty equal to 20 percent of the annual license fee shall be imposed. No renewal license shall be granted after December 31, but such application shall be treated as an initial application, and the applicant shall be required to comply with all rules and regulations for the granting of licenses as if no previous license had been issued to licensee.
(b) Except for temporary licenses or permits that may be granted pursuant to this chapter, all licenses granted under this chapter shall be for the full calendar year or for the number of months (or portion thereof) remaining in the calendar year. License fees shall not be prorated for any reason, and license fees shall not be refundable for any reason.
(c) Failure to furnish complete information in the renewal application will delay the issuance of the license. The failure to furnish complete information within 30 days after being requested to do so by the county clerk may be grounds to deny the renewal application.
(Ord. No. 2022-3, § I, 7-11-2022; Ord. No. 23-1, § I, 1-9-2023)
155:
(a) No license shall be issued for the sale of any distilled spirits in or within 100 yards of any church building or within 200 yards of any school building, educational building, school grounds, or college campus.
(b) No license shall be issued for the sale of malt beverage(s) and/or wine by the package for a location that is within 100 yards of any school building, school grounds or college campus (the preceding regulation shall not apply to any location for which a license has been issued prior to July 1, 1981, nor to the renewal of such license, nor shall the preceding regulation apply at any location for which a new license is applied for if the sale of malt beverage(s) and/or wine was lawful at such location at any time during the 12 months immediately preceding such application); provided that, nothing in the preceding regulation shall prohibit a grocery store licensed for the retail sale of only malt beverages and/or wine for consumption off the premises from selling malt beverage(s) and/or wine within 100 yards of any school building, school grounds, or college campus, where so permitted by resolution or ordinance of the county or municipality (as used in this subparagraph, the term "grocery store" means a retail establishment which has a total retail floor space of at least 10,000 square feet of which at least 85 percent is reserved for the sale of food and other nonalcoholic items, conducts all of its sales inside the building containing its retail floor space, and meets such other criteria as may be required by the governing authority.
(c) No license shall be issued for the sale of malt beverage(s) and/or wine by the package for a location that is within 100 yards of any alcoholic treatment center owned and operated by the state or by any county or municipal government (the preceding regulation shall not apply to any business having a license in effect on July 1, 1981).
(d) No license shall be issued for the sale any alcoholic beverages for consumption on the premises within 100 yards of any housing authority property (the preceding regulation shall not apply at any location for which a license has been issued prior to July 1, 2000, nor to the renewal of such license, nor shall the preceding regulation apply at any location for which a new license is applied for if the sale of alcoholic beverages for consumption on the premises was lawful at such location at any time during the 12 months immediately prior to such application; and as used in the preceding regulation, the term "housing authority property" means any property containing 300 housing units or fewer owned or operated by a housing authority created by Article 1 of Chapter 3 of Title 8, the "Housing Authorities Law," O.C.G.A.).
(e) For purposes of this chapter, distances shall be measured by the most direct route of travel on the ground.
(Ord. No. 2022-3, § I, 7-11-2022; Ord. No. 23-1, § I, 1-9-2023)
156:
(a) A license shall be issued for a calendar year and shall expire on December 31 of the year for which issued regardless of the date issued, and there shall be no rebate, proration or refund of any annual license fee.
(b) The fee(s) for any license issued pursuant to this chapter shall be in the amount as determined and set by the governing authority pursuant to resolution or ordinance, and any and all such fees shall be tendered to the county clerk upon submission of the application, in the form of certified funds or cash.
(c) A license may be issued only on written application, and the county clerk shall provide the application form required by this chapter, which shall include but not be limited to the applicant's full name, address, telephone number. The fee for a license shall be tendered upon submission of the application to the county clerk.
(d) Each application for a license may be issued a license only by the governing authority while in session. Each application for a license shall not be considered until:
(1) Notice of the application has been posted by the county clerk at the courthouse door of Tattnall County for at least ten days prior to the governing authority's consideration of the application, and
(2) The county sheriff, or any of his or her deputies, has reviewed the application and given a report to the governing authority regarding the applicant and location proposed by the application.
Only the initial application for a new license shall be required to post the notice required by this chapter. Yearly renewals of a license, which include the same licensee and location, do not require the posting of notice.
(e) Where an application is issued and a license issued in connection therewith, such license shall be issued for only one licensee and location, and such license shall not be transferrable either as to the location or licensee, except as may be otherwise permitted by this chapter.
(f) A licensee shall not have any vested rights in a license, and a license shall not be renewable as a matter of right. Applications must be made annually for the governing authority's consideration if a licensee desires to continue operation from year to year. Each application shall be considered as a new application, except insofar as the requirements of posting a notice may be concerned, even though the applicant may have a license for the same location for the previous year.
(g) The standards to be applied by the governing authority, acting in its judicial capacity to grant or deny a license, shall include whether, in the best judgment of the governing authority, the applicant, based on all information obtained in the application process, possesses the qualities of sound judgment and discretion necessary for one who dispenses alcoholic beverages to the public generally.
(Ord. No. 2022-3, § I, 7-11-2022; Ord. No. 23-1, § I, 1-9-2023)
157:
Each licensee shall display all licenses issued to such licensee prominently and at all times on the premises for which all such licenses are issued.
(Ord. No. 2022-3, § I, 7-11-2022; Ord. No. 23-1, § I, 1-9-2023)
158:
Any code enforcement officer of the county or the county sheriff, or any of his or her deputies shall have the authority to inspect any business or premises licensed under this chapter during the hours in which the business or premises is open for business. These inspections shall be made for the purpose of verifying compliance with the requirements of this chapter and state law.
(Ord. No. 2022-3, § I, 7-11-2022; Ord. No. 23-1, § I, 1-9-2023)
159:
Notwithstanding any other provision of this chapter, an unsuccessful applicant for a license shall not be authorized to re-apply for a license until 180 days have elapsed from the date that the governing authority's decision to deny such license becomes final. Notwithstanding any other provision of this chapter, a licensee whose license is revoked by governing authority shall not be eligible to re-apply for a license until one year has elapsed from the date that the governing authority's decision to revoke such license becomes final.
(Ord. No. 2022-3, § I, 7-11-2022; Ord. No. 23-1, § I, 1-9-2023)
160:
(a) No person under 18 years of age shall be employed in or about the premises of any person licensed to sell alcoholic beverages.
(b) It shall be unlawful for a person under 21 years of age to attempt to purchase an alcoholic beverage or for any person to purchase an alcoholic beverage for a person under 21 years of age.
(c) It shall be unlawful for a person under 21 years of age to exhibit faked, forged, or borrowed credentials in an effort to obtain an alcoholic beverage to which he is not legally entitled.
(d) It shall be unlawful for a person under 21 years of age, other than an employee employed by a licensed person, to have an open container of any alcoholic beverage in his possession.
(e) It shall be a violation for any licensee not to require and properly analyze the identification of a person to ensure that any person under 21 years of age is not sold, served, or has in his possession any alcoholic beverage while in a licensed business or premises; provided that, a licensed employee working in a licensed business or premises may have in his possession any alcoholic beverage for the purpose of selling or serving such alcoholic beverages. The term "identification" as used in this section, shall mean any document issued by a governmental agency containing a description of the person, a photograph, and giving such person's date of birth, and includes, without being limited to, a passport, military identification card, driver's license or state identification card.
(Ord. No. 2022-3, § I, 7-11-2022; Ord. No. 23-1, § I, 1-9-2023)
162:
No licensed retail dealer shall purchase any alcoholic beverage from any person other than a licensed wholesale dealer. No licensed wholesale dealer shall sell any alcoholic beverages to any person other than a licensed retail dealer.
(Ord. No. 2022-3, § I, 7-11-2022; Ord. No. 23-1, § I, 1-9-2023)
163:
(a) It shall be unlawful for a licensee, his agent or employee to permit any disturbance of the peace, any obscenity, or any lewd, immoral or improper behavior, conduct or practices in the licensed business or premises, or to operate the licensed business or premises in such a manner as to create a nuisance.
(b) It shall be unlawful for any licensee, his agent or employee to fail to report to the county sheriff any disturbance which occurs immediately outside his business or premises, or in the parking facilities of his business or premises, of which he has knowledge.
(c) It shall be the duty and responsibility of the licensee, his agent, or employee to report to the county sheriff any usage or possession of illegal drugs or narcotics and to report any unlawful conduct of any nature which occurs on the licensed premises, of which he has knowledge.
(d) It shall be unlawful for any licensee, his agent or employee, to fail to assist any law enforcement officer in the performance of the officer's duties while the officer is in or on a licensed business or premises.
(Ord. No. 2022-3, § I, 7-11-2022; Ord. No. 23-1, § I, 1-9-2023)
164:
Consumption or sale of alcoholic beverages in open areas or on decks or patios is not permitted unless a licensee's business or premises is licensed for the retail sale of alcoholic beverages for beverage purposes by the drink for consumption only on the premises and such licensee complies with the following regulations:
(1) The open area, patio or deck must be enclosed in a manner that directs ingress and egress by the public through a single entrance only through the licensed business or premises (the purpose of this requirement is to prevent a customer from leaving the open area, patio or deck with an alcoholic beverage without the licensee's knowledge).
(2) The open area, patio or deck shall be enclosed by a structure at least 42 inches in height as measured from the floor of the open area, patio or deck, and such structure must meet all building code requirements of the county.
(3) Any licensee desiring to obtain approval for open area, patio or deck sales must submit to the county a complete set of plans that will be reviewed and approved on an individual basis by appropriate county officials and/or employee(s), and all plans and construction pursuant to such plans shall meet the requirements of the Code, as well as all applicable state health, life safety and fire code. Only upon satisfactory completion of a final inspection will the county approve of any open area, patio or deck sales.
(4) Any structure or area set aside for open area, patio or deck sales shall not contain a number of square feet that represents an amount greater than 40 percent of the existing seating area of the licensed business or premises.
(5) Loudspeakers or other amplifiers of sound shall not be permitted upon the open areas, patios or decks of any licensed business or premises.
(Ord. No. 2022-3, § I, 7-11-2022; Ord. No. 23-1, § I, 1-9-2023)
165:
(a) It shall be unlawful for any person to drink any alcoholic beverage or other intoxicating beverage at any public place within the unincorporated area of county, or for any person to have in his or her possession any unsealed or opened container with such intoxicating beverage in it at any public place within the unincorporated area of the county, except as may be otherwise permitted by this chapter or the Code.
(b) It shall be unlawful for any person to drink or possess any alcoholic beverage upon real property of the county that is used as a public park, playground or school.
(c) It shall be unlawful for any person to drink any alcoholic beverage in any automobile on the roads or streets of the county, whether such automobile is moving or parked.
(d) Brown bag establishments shall be prohibited within the unincorporated area of the county.
(Ord. No. 2022-3, § I, 7-11-2022; Ord. No. 23-1, § I, 1-9-2023)
166:
(a) No outdoor advertising promoting the sale or consumption of alcoholic beverages shall be permitted on the exterior of any business or premises that is licensed for wholesale or retail sale of alcoholic beverages or any business or premises that is licensed for the sale of alcoholic beverages for beverage purposes by the drink for consumption only on the premises.
(b) Any indoor sign or display promoting the sale or consumption of alcoholic beverages may be visible from the exterior of any business or premises that is licensed for wholesale or retail sale of alcoholic beverages or any business or premises that is licensed for the sale of alcoholic beverages for beverage purposes by the drink for consumption only on the premises, subject to the limitations as otherwise set forth in this chapter.
(Ord. No. 2022-3, § I, 7-11-2022; Ord. No. 23-1, § I, 1-9-2023)
167:
No licensee, or his or her agents or employees, shall engage in any of the following practices in connection with the sale or other disposition of alcoholic beverages for beverage purposes by the drink for consumption only on the premises:
(1) Advertising "Happy Hour" through any form of media, including, but not limited to, newspapers, magazines, electronics, radio, television and internet, or
(2) Outdoor advertising or signs promoting "Happy Hour" on the exterior of any licensed premises or on the windows or elsewhere on the licensed business or premises that may be viewed from the outside.
(Ord. No. 2022-3, § I, 7-11-2022; Ord. No. 23-1, § I, 1-9-2023)
168:
(a) The business or premises of each licensee shall have a clearly marked point(s) of entry.
(b) The business or premises of each licensee shall have point(s) of entry that are clearly visible from a public street; however, this requirement shall not apply to hotels or where the point of entry of the licensed business or premises is in a shopping center or business building.
(c) The business or premises of each licensee shall ensure that, at all points of entry, there are clear windows and doors. Further, the business or premises of each licensee must maintain clear windows and doors for any cashier's cage within the premises, or other internally enclosed space.
(d) The business or premises of each licensee, including those entirely enclosed in another building, such as a restaurant located in a hotel, must keep all windows and doors free of visual obstructions so that the interior of such business or premises is clearly visible from the exterior. No tinting, shades, curtains, blinds or other devices shall be used to obstruct the view into such business or premises, but tinting, shades, curtains, blinds, and other devices may be used to reduce sun glare so long as such measures do not impede visual access to the business or premises.
(e) The business or premises of each licensee shall operate with an adequate level of internal lighting, so as to ensure visual access from the exterior and safety to law enforcement or other emergency responders, 24 hours a day, seven days a week. External lighting cannot be solely used to meet this requirement.
(Ord. No. 2022-3, § I, 7-11-2022; Ord. No. 23-1, § I, 1-9-2023)
169:
(a) No license application shall be considered until the county clerk deems it complete as set forth in this chapter.
(b) If a license application is denied, the applicant for such license cannot apply for another license for a period of 180 days from the date of the denial.
(Ord. No. 2022-3, § I, 7-11-2022; Ord. No. 23-1, § I, 1-9-2023)
171:
(a) A licensed retail dealer of beer, malt beverages and/or wine by the package shall not furnish, offer to sell, sell, give away or otherwise distribute any of the foregoing alcoholic beverages except as follows:
(1) As permitted by state law;
(2) Between 6:00 a.m. and 2:00 a.m., Monday through Saturday, but with the limitation of between 6:00 a.m. Saturday through 11:59 p.m. Saturday; or
(3) Between 11:00 a.m. Sunday to 11:59 p.m. Sunday.
(b) A licensed retail dealer of distilled spirits shall not open its place of business or furnish, offer to sell, sell, give away or otherwise distribute any alcoholic beverage at any of the following times:
(1) In violation of state law;
(2) In violation of a special order of the commissioner of the Georgia Department of Revenue;
(3) Sundays prior to 11:00 a.m., except as otherwise provided in OCGA § 3-3-7; or
(4) Any other day prior to 8:00 a.m.
(c) A licensed retail dealer of beer, malt beverages and/ or wine by the drink for beverage purposes for consumption on the premises only shall not furnish, offer to sell, sell, give away or otherwise distribute any of the foregoing alcoholic beverages except as follows:
(1) As permitted by state law;
(2) Between 10:00 a.m. and 2:00 a.m., Monday through Saturday, with the limitation of between 10:00 a.m. Saturday through 11:59 p.m. Saturday; or
(3) Between 11:00 a.m. Sunday and 11:59 p.m. Sunday.
(Ord. No. 2022-3, § I, 7-11-2022; Ord. No. 23-1, § I, 1-9-2023; Ord. No. 2023-3, § I, 11-6-2023)
172:
(a) A retail dealer of beer, malt beverages and/or wine by the package may apply for and obtain a Sunday sales license for the retail sale of beer, malt beverages and/or wine by the package upon due qualification for and payment for such license, as set forth in this chapter.
(b) A retail dealer of beer, malt beverages, wine and/or distilled spirits for beverage purposes by the drink for consumption only on the premises may apply for and obtain a Sunday sales license for the retail sale of beer, malt beverages, wine and/or distilled spirits for beverage purposes by the drink for consumption only on the premises, upon the occurrence of the following:
(1) Due qualification for and payment for such license, as set forth in this chapter; and
(2) Showing to the satisfaction of the county manager or administrator, or his or her designee, that such retail dealer derives at least 50 percent of its total annual gross sales from the sale of prepared meals or food in all of the combined retail outlets of the individual establishments where food is served and in any licensed establishment which derives at least 50 percent of its total annual gross income from the rental of rooms for overnight lodging.
(Ord. No. 2022-3, § I, 7-11-2022; Ord. No. 23-1, § I, 1-9-2023)
174:
Any person who violates any provision of this chapter shall be punishable by a fine not exceed a fine of $1,000.00, or six months' imprisonment, or both; provided that, the judge shall probate not less than 120 days of any sentence imposed, except as otherwise provided by general law, and shall not exceed the maximum punishment specified by the this chapter. In the event a sentence is revoked, a defendant shall not serve more than 60 days in the county jail.
(Ord. No. 2022-3, § I, 7-11-2022; Ord. No. 23-1, § I, 1-9-2023)
175:
(a) In addition to any other punishment or penalty set forth in this chapter, unless prohibited by law, any person who violates any provision of this chapter may be cited for violating any part of this chapter and tried by the court of competent jurisdiction in the county, and upon conviction for any such violation, be punished as authorized by or provided for in the Code.
(b) Notwithstanding any other penalty or remedy authorized by this chapter or law, continuing violations of this chapter are hereby further declared to be a public nuisance, harmful to the public health, safety, and welfare, and are subject to abatement or injunction by the court of competent jurisdiction in the county.
(Ord. No. 2022-3, § I, 7-11-2022; Ord. No. 23-1, § I, 1-9-2023)
178:
A license for a retail dealer or wholesale dealer for the sale of beer, malt beverages and/or wine may be granted by the governing authority upon the terms and conditions as provided in this chapter. Further, a license for the retail sale of beer, malt beverages and/or wine for beverage purposes by the drink for consumption only on the premises may be granted by the governing authority upon the terms and conditions as provided in this chapter. No person will be issued a license for the sale of beer, malt beverages and/or wine, where the same is sold in the original packages, and a license for the sale of beer, malt beverages and/or wine for beverage purposes by the drink for consumption only on the premises at the same location.
(Ord. No. 2022-3, § I, 7-11-2022; Ord. No. 23-1, § I, 1-9-2023)
179:
Before any license permitted under this article is granted by the governing authority, the applicant shall comply with all regulations adopted by the governing authority applicable to such licenses and pay the applicable license fee by certified bank check in an amount set by resolution or ordinance by the governing authority and maintained as a public document by the county clerk.
(Ord. No. 2022-3, § I, 7-11-2022; Ord. No. 23-1, § I, 1-9-2023)
180:
(a) There is hereby levied and imposed upon the sale of beer and malt beverages within the unincorporated area of the county a specific excise tax as follows:
(1) where beer and malt beverages are sold in or from a barrel or bulk container, a tax of $6.00 on each container sold containing not more than 15½ gallons and a proportionate tax at the same rate on all fractional parts of 15½ gallons; and
(2) where beer and malt beverages are sold in bottles, cans, or other containers, except barrel or bulk containers, a tax of $0.05 per 12 ounces and a proportionate tax at the same rate on all fractional parts of 12 ounces.
(b) The excise taxes provided for in this section shall be imposed upon and shall be paid by the licensed wholesale dealer in beer and malt beverages. Each wholesale dealer selling beer and malt beverages within the unincorporated area of the county shall file a report with the county by the 10th day of each month showing for the preceding calendar month the exact quantities of beer and malt beverages, by size and type of container, sold during the month within the unincorporated area of the county. Each wholesale dealer shall remit to the county clerk on the 10th day of the month after the calendar month in which such sales were made the amount of excise tax due in accordance with this section.
(Ord. No. 2022-3, § I, 7-11-2022; Ord. No. 23-1, § I, 1-9-2023)
181:
(a) There is hereby levied and imposed upon the sale of wine within the unincorporated area of the county, a specific excise tax in the amount of $0.22 per liter and a proportionate tax at the same rate on all fractional parts of a liter.
(b) The taxes imposed by this section shall not be levied with respect to:
(1) Wine sold to and used by established and recognized churches and synagogues for use in sacramental services only;
(2) Any sale of wine which is exempt from taxation by the state under the Constitution of the United States;
(3) Wine sold to persons outside the state for resale or consumption outside the state; or
(4) Wine which contains less than one-half of one percent alcohol.
(c) The excise taxes as provided for in this section shall be imposed upon and paid by the licensed wholesale dealer in wine in the unincorporated area of the county, and each wholesale dealer of wine within the unincorporated area of the county shall file a report with the county by the 10th day of each month showing for the preceding calendar month the exact quantities of wine, by size and type of container, sold during the month within the unincorporated area of the county. Each wholesale dealer shall remit to the county on the 10th day of the month after the calendar month in which such sales were made the amount of excise tax due in accordance with the manner or procedure described in section 10-68.
(Ord. No. 2022-3, § I, 7-11-2022; Ord. No. 23-1, § I, 1-9-2023)
182:
Beer, malt beverages and/or wine shall not be distributed, sold or possessed for the purposes of sale without a license granted by the governing authority. A separate application must be made, and a separate license must be obtained to sell beer, malt beverages and/or wine for each premises where beer, malt beverages and/or wine is sold at retail or wholesale, or where beer, malt beverages and/or wine is sold at retail for beverage purposes by the drink for consumption only on the premises.
(Ord. No. 2022-3, § I, 7-11-2022; Ord. No. 23-1, § I, 1-9-2023)
183:
A license for the retail sale of beer, malt beverages and/or wine by the drink for beverage purposes for consumption on the premises only shall be issued only in conjunction with a restaurant, hotel or motel, or a publicly owned facility, as defined in Chapter 8 of Title 3, O.C.G.A.
(Ord. No. 2022-3, § I, 7-11-2022; Ord. No. 23-1, § I, 1-9-2023)
184:
(a) Where a license is issued for the retail sale of beer, malt beverages and/or wine by the drink for beverage purposes for consumption on the premises only, in conjunction with a restaurant, the licensee of such license shall submit quarterly written reports to the county clerk, as more particularly set forth herein.
(b) Every report shall be post marked on or before the last day of the calendar month after the calendar quarter.
(c) Every report shall be in a form recognized and accepted by certified public accountants and shall utilize common and generally recognized accounting principles and shall be submitted under oath. False information in any report may result in the prosecution under O.C.G.A. § 16-10-20 by a court of competent jurisdiction.
(d) Every report shall clearly indicate all sales receipts of the restaurant for food and alcoholic beverages, and for reporting purposes, food shall be defined as all edible substances appropriate for human consumption as detennined by the health department inspecting restaurants as sold or provided to the public in a restaurant in the unincorporated area of the county. Food shall not be construed to include olives, cherries, limes, lemons, salt, pepper, pineapples, celery, tomato juice, or any other fruit or vegetable, or any dairy product such as ice cream, cream, yogurt or milk, or any soft drink, water, tonic water or non-alcoholic carbonated or non-carbonated beverages, when such items are used in any alcoholic beverage or mixed drink as an essential part of the beverage, mixed drink, or as a garnish thereon.
(e) Notwithstanding anything in this chapter to the contrary, if any report of a restaurant shows that its sales receipts for food comprise less than 50 percent of a restaurant's total gross sales receipts in any quarter of a calendar year, then, thereafter, the governing authority may consider such event as grounds for suspension or revocation.
(Ord. No. 2022-3, § I, 7-11-2022; Ord. No. 23-1, § I, 1-9-2023)
185:
No beer, malt beverages and/or wine shall be delivered to any licensed retail dealer except by a licensed wholesale dealer, who shall make such deliveries by a vehicle owned by the wholesaler, with wholesaler's name clearly marked on the outside of the vehicle.
(Ord. No. 2022-3, § I, 7-11-2022; Ord. No. 23-1, § I, 1-9-2023)
186:
No person with a license for the retail sale of beer, malt beverages or wine shall permit on his premises any coin operated amusement machine, including but not limited to a slot machine, mechanical music box or pinball machine, or any form of electronic or mechanical game machine or coin-operated device, which might be used for entertainment or amusement purposes, except pursuant to applicable state law.
(Ord. No. 2022-3, § I, 7-11-2022; Ord. No. 23-1, § I, 1-9-2023)
189:
A license for the retail sale or wholesale sale of distilled spirits by the original package may be granted by the governing authority upon the terms and conditions as provided in this article. No person may hold a license for the sale of distilled spirits by the package and a license for the sale of distilled spirits by the drink for beverage purposes for consumption on the premises only at the same location.
(Ord. No. 2022-3, § I, 7-11-2022; Ord. No. 23-1, § I, 1-9-2023)

(a) Before any license permitted under this article is granted by the governing authority, the applicant shall comply with all regulations adopted by the governing authority applicable to such licenses and pay the applicable license fee by certified bank check in an amount set by resolution or ordinance by the governing authority and maintained as a public document by the county clerk.
(b) In addition to the license fees established by this chapter, there is hereby levied and imposed a specific excise tax on the sale of distilled spirits by the package within the unincorporated area of the county, in the amount of $0.22 per liter of distilled spirits, excluding fortified wine, and a proportionate tax at the same rate on all fractional parts of a liter. The excise tax as provided for in this section shall be imposed upon and shall be paid by the licensed wholesale dealer in distilled spirits by the package. The payment and filing of returns requirements of such wholesale dealer shall be in accordance with the manner or procedure set forth in section 10-68.
(Ord. No. 2022-3, § I, 7-11-2022; Ord. No. 23-1, § I, 1-9-2023)
191:
(a) All applications for licenses under this article, both original and renewal, must be accompanied by a full and complete statement under oath of information describing any and all interests, as defined by state law, in the person licensed or to be licensed. This information shall include the names and addresses of any person who has any ownership interest in the person licensed or to be licensed and the size of such interest; the specific street address of any other premises which is authorized for retail sale of alcoholic beverages by the package in which the person licensed or to be licensed has any ownership interest; detailed description of the ownership or leasehold of premises where the person licensed or to be licensed is or will be operating, including but not limited to an executed copy of the vesting deed or lease; and the name and address of any owner and lessor of the premises in which the person licensed or to be licensed is or will be operating.
(b) Any change in the information required in subsection (a) must be filed with the county clerk when the change occurs, and failure to do so within a period of 30 days of such change shall be grounds for denial, suspension or revocation, as applicable under the circumstances, by the governing authority.
(Ord. No. 2022-3, § I, 7-11-2022; Ord. No. 23-1, § I, 1-9-2023)

(Ord. No. 2022-3, § I, 7-11-2022; Ord. No. 23-1, § I, 1-9-2023)

A license for the retail sale of distilled spirits for beverage purposes by the drink for consumption only on the premises may be granted by the governing authority upon the terms and conditions as provided in this article.
(Ord. No. 2022-3, § I, 7-11-2022; Ord. No. 23-1, § I, 1-9-2023)
199:
Before any license permitted under this article is granted by the governing authority, the applicant shall comply with all regulations adopted by the governing authority applicable to such license and pay the applicable license fee by certified bank check in an amount set by resolution or ordinance by the governing authority and maintained as a public document by the county clerk.
(Ord. No. 2022-3, § I, 7-11-2022; Ord. No. 23-1, § I, 1-9-2023)

A license for the retail sale of distilled spirits for beverage purposes by the drink for consumption only on the premises shall be issued only in conjunction with a restaurant, hotel or motel, or a publicly owned facility, as defined by Chapter 8 of Title 3, O.C.G.A.
