214:
This article shall be referred to as the "Animal Control Ordinance" for unincorporated area of Tattnall County. The purpose of this article is to provide for the humane treatment of animals by regulating the control of animals within unincorporated area Tattnall County; to promote the public health, safety and general welfare of the citizens of the county; and to provide the means by which the proper officers and officials can implement, administer and enforce this article, including but not limited to the abatement of nuisances arising from or in connection with this article. This article sets forth necessary controls on the unrestrained activities of animals which threaten the safety and pleasantness of roads public places, and all areas of unincorporated Tattnall County. The lack of knowledge or intent is not a defense in the violation of this article.
(Ord. No. 2025-2, § I, 4-7-2025)
216:
The owner of animals shall be responsible for correcting or abating any nuisance that may arise from the keeping thereof. No person shall own or possess or harbor any animal which howls, barks, or emits audible sounds that are plainly audible or disturbing and which are of such character, intensity and duration as to disturb the peace and quiet of the neighborhood. For the purpose of this article, "barking dog" shall mean a dog that barks, bays, cries, howls or makes any other noise continuously and/or incessantly for a period of ten minutes or barks intermittently for one-half hour or more to the disturbance of any person at any time day or night regardless of whether the dog is physically situated in or upon private property; provided, however, that a dog shall not be deemed a "barking dog" for purposes of this regulation, if at the time the dog is barking or making any other noise, a person is trespassing or threatening to trespass upon private property in or upon which the dog is situated or for any other legitimate cause which teased or provoked the dog.
(Ord. No. 2025-2, § I, 4-7-2025)
217:
(a) Animal control officers are responsible for administering and enforcing this article and chapter and are authorized to issue and serve citations for appearance before the court of competent jurisdiction of the county for violations of the provisions of this article and chapter.
(b) Animal control officers who are responsible for administering and enforcing this article and chapter are authorized to investigate and report to the proper officials for appropriate prosecution, any violations of this chapter relating to cruelty to animals or any violations of the Georgia Animal Protection Act (O.C.G.A. § 4-11-1 et seq., as amended).
(Ord. No. 2025-2, § I, 4-7-2025)
218:
Except as otherwise required by state law, any judicial or quasi-judicial proceeding initiated in connection with a violation of this article or chapter, whether civil or criminal in nature, will be brought in the court of competent jurisdiction in the county.
(Ord. No. 2025-2, § I, 4-7-2025)
219:
Except as otherwise required by state law, any person who violates any provision of this article or chapter shall be punishable by a fine not exceed a fine of $1,000.00 or a term in incarceration not to exceed six months or both; provided that, the judge shall probate not less than 120 days of any sentence imposed, except as otherwise provided by general law, and shall not exceed the maximum punishment specified by this article. In the event a sentence is revoked, a defendant or violator shall not serve more than 60 days in the county jail.
(Ord. No. 2025-2, § I, 4-7-2025)
220:
Notwithstanding any other penalty or remedy authorized by this article, chapter or state law, continuing violations of this article or chapter are hereby further declared to be a public nuisance, harmful to the public health, safety, and welfare, and are subject to abatement or injunction in and by the court of competent jurisdiction in the county or through any other legal or equitable remedy allowed by law.
(Ord. No. 2025-2, § I, 4-7-2025)
221:
(a) Except to the extent otherwise provided in this article or chapter, and except to the extent otherwise authorized or allowed by law, no person, except the animal's owner or possessor, a person authorized by the owner or possessor, a licensed veterinarian or an employee, agent or a person acting pursuant to any privilege or authority granted pursuant to federal, state or local law, ordinance, rule or regulation, shall kill any animal within the county. No person shall intentionally kill any animal in any manner or by any method or means which is inhumane or which causes such animal unnecessary pain or suffering under the circumstances.
(b) It shall be unlawful for any person or custodian of any animal to permit or cause unsanitary, offensive or dangerous conditions by virtue of the size or number of domesticated animals maintained at a single location or due to the inadequacy of the facilities.
(c) No person shall release or abandon any domesticated animal, either alive or dead, upon any public or upon the property of any person.
(d) No person shall knowingly by neglect, omission or act allow any domesticated animal to endure unnecessary pain or suffering or aid or assist in the causation of any unnecessary pain, suffering or injury by any such animal.
(e) No person shall by neglect, omission or act leave any poisonous or toxic substance in a manner that permits and domesticated animal to come into contact with such poisonous or toxic substance.
(Ord. No. 2025-2, § I, 4-7-2025)
222:
Any enclosure used for the keeping of an animal or animals outside of a building shall be kept at a minimum distance of 100 feet from any occupied building, except the dwelling the owner or possessor.
(Ord. No. 2025-2, § I, 4-7-2025)
223:
Any housing or enclosure used for the keeping of animals shall be well-drained, free from accumulation of animal excrement and objectionable odors, and otherwise clean and sanitary.
(Ord. No. 2025-2, § I, 4-7-2025)
224:
Notwithstanding any other provision of this article or chapter, licensed veterinarians, state and local law enforcement officers or those authorized by the county to administer and enforce the provisions of this chapter or article, and all federal, state and local governmental employees while acting within scope of their authority are empowered to induce the death of any disabled animal by appropriate humane methods, preferably by means of euthanasia. Such officer shall be held harmless for such actions as they relate to humane destruction of any such animal.
(Ord. No. 2025-2, § I, 4-7-2025)
226:
Notwithstanding anything in this article or chapter to the contrary, it shall be unlawful for any animal or livestock to run loose or at large within the unincorporated Tattnall County on any property without permission of the owner of such property.
(Ord. No. 2025-2, § I, 4-7-2025)
228:
(a) Any animal may be seized by an animal control officer where there is a violation of this chapter or article on two or more occasions during any twelve-month period of time, or where there is a violation of state or federal law regarding animals, and in such event, the seizure shall be conclusive evidence of abandonment and forfeiture of the animal by its owner and possessor. Following the seizure of the animal, it may be delivered to the Tattnall County Animal Shelter or any other appropriate agency or entity for disposition, disposal or destruction.
(b) Any animal that has been seized under the provisions of this section shall be returned to its owner or possessor upon such owner's or possessor's: 1) compliance with provisions of this article, 2) payment of seizure costs, which include boarding of the animal the rate of $50.00 per day, plus a pickup fee of $50.00, and 3) payment of the current cost of a rabies vaccination, if the animal's owner or possessor does not produce proof of a current rabies vaccination. If the animal's owner or possessor has not complied with the provisions of this article within the 12 days of the date of seizure of the animal, the county is authorized to dispose of or destroy the animal.
(Ord. No. 2025-2, § I, 4-7-2025)
229:
(a) The owner or possessor of an animal seized pursuant to this article or chapter, or for violation of O.C.G.A. § 16-12-4, as amended, or O.C.G.A. § 4-11-10, as amended, or any other statute, law or ordinance requiring humane treatment of animals, who shall plead guilty or nolo contendere to any such offense or who shall be found guilty of such offense shall be conclusively deemed to have abandoned and forfeited such animal. Such animal thereafter may be delivered to the Tattnall County Animal Shelter or other appropriate agency or entity for disposition, disposal or destruction.
(b) The failure of the owner or possessor of any such animal, that has been seized pursuant to the provisions of this article or chapter, to strictly comply with any condition, limitation, prohibition or restriction imposed with respect to such animal by a court of competent jurisdiction, shall be conclusively deemed to have abandoned and forfeited such animal, and thereafter such animal may be delivered to the Tattnall County Animal Shelter or other appropriate agency or entity for disposition, disposal or destruction.
(Ord. No. 2025-2, § I, 4-7-2025)
233:
(a) Generally. Every dog and cat shall be inoculated by its owner or possessor.
(b) Tag and collar. Every dog shall wear a collar with a badge showing the fact of its inoculation.
(c) Exemptions. The provisions of this section shall not be construed to apply to dogs whose owners or possessors are non-residents temporarily within the unincorporated area of the county, nor to dogs brought in the unincorporated area of the county for the purpose of participating in any dog show, nor to seeing eye dogs properly trained to assist blind persons when such dogs are actually being used by blind persons for the purpose of aiding them in going from place to place.
(Ord. No. 2025-2, § I, 4-7-2025)
234:
(a) It shall be unlawful for the owner or possessor of any dog to refuse or fail to provide such dog with sufficient wholesome and nutritious food, humane care, potable water adequate shelter (24 hours, seven days a week) and treatment needed to prevent suffering.
(b) It shall be unlawful for any person or possessor of any dog to permit or cause unsanitary, offensive or dangerous conditions by virtue of the size or number of dogs maintained at a single location or due to the inadequacy of the facilities.
(c) It shall be unlawful for the owner or possessor of any dog to willfully abandon such animal on any street, road, lane, alleys, public place or private property within the unincorporated area of the county.
(d) It shall be unlawful for a person to allow any dog in their possession or under their control to run at large upon the streets, roads, lanes, public places or alleys of within the unincorporated area of the county.

(Ord. No. 2025-2, § I, 4-7-2025)
235:
(a) The following definitions shall apply in the interpretation and enforcement of this code section, unless otherwise specifically stated:
Direct point chaining means a dog attached to a stationary object by a chain, cable or similar device commonly used for the size and type of dog involved.
Electronic animal confinement system shall mean a commercially produced, functioning electronic fence which utilizes an invisible electrically generated perimeter, in which the animal within the perimeter wears an electronic collar that produces an electric shock when the animal approaches or exceeds the perimeter.
(b) It shall be the duty of every owner of a dog to ensure that the dog is securely and humanely enclosed within a proper enclosure as a means of primary restraint. Such enclosure must be securely locked and any time the dog is left unattended. When outside the proper enclosure but on the owner's property, it shall be the duty of every owner of a dog to ensure that the dog is humanely secured by a leash or lead and under the control of a responsible and competent person; or off leash but under the direct control of a responsible and competent person who is physically present with the dog, provided that such dog is obedient to that person's command.
(c) Any dog that is housed outside of its owner's house shall be housed in a proper enclosure that complies with the provisions of this Code.
(d) Direct point chaining of a dog is prohibited, except for limited periods of four hours or less in humane conditions.
(e) As a secondary means of restraint to or within a proper enclosure, a dog may be attached to a running cable line or trolley system that conforms with the following guidelines:
(1) Only one dog may be attached to each running cable line or trolley system;
(2) Cables attaching the dog to the running cable line or trolley system must be made of a substance which cannot be chewed through by the dog and shall not weigh more than 25 percent of the body weight of the dog tethered;
(3) A running cable line or trolley system must have a swivel installed at each end and be attached to a stationary object that cannot be moved by the dog;
(4) The running cable line or trolley system must be at least 15 feet in length and positioned at sufficient distance from any other objects to prohibit the tangling of the cable/lead line; must not extend over an object or an edge that could result in injury of strangulation of the dog; and must be of sufficient distance from any fence as to prohibit the dog from access to the fence;
(5) The length of the lead line from the running cable line or trolley system to the dog's harness should allow access to the maximum available exercise area and allow the animal free access to food, water, and shelter. In no event shall the length of the lead line allow for access to less than the square footage allowed within a proper enclosure; and
(6) The lead line must be attached to a properly fitted harness not used for the display of a current rabies tag and other identification. Collars are prohibited for the purpose of securing a dog to a running cable line or trolley system.
(f) If an electronic animal confinement system is used to confine a dog, it shall provide a properly fitted and working signal device that will be worn by the dog to be enclosed.
(Ord. No. 2025-2, § I, 4-7-2025)
236:
Whenever any dog bites a person, the owner of such animal shall immediately notify an animal control officer, who shall order the animal held on the owner's premises or shall order the animal impounded for quarantine, at the owner's expense, for a period of time as determined in the sole discretion of an official with the Tattnall County Health Department or an animal control officer. At the end of any impound period, if a veterinarian is satisfied that the dog is free from rabies, the dog may be released from impound.
(Ord. No. 2025-2, § I, 4-7-2025)
239:
(a) Upon receiving a report of a dangerous dog within the unincorporated area of the county, an animal control officer shall make such investigation regarding such report as may be necessary to carry out the provisions of this article.
(b) When an animal control officer determines that a dog as a dangerous dog, within 72 hours of such determination, such officer shall notify the dog's owner in writing by certified mail to the owner's last known address of such classification or reclassification. Such notice shall be deemed complete mailing.
(c) As used herein, the term "dangerous dog" shall mean any dog which without provocation bites, inflicts serious injury upon, or attacks a human being on public or private property.
(Ord. No. 2025-2, § I, 4-7-2025)
241:
(a) It is unlawful for an owner to have or possess within the unincorporated area of the county a dangerous dog without a certificate of registration issued in accordance with the provisions of this section.
(b) Subject to the additional requirements of subsection (c) of this section for dangerous dogs, an animal control officer will issue a certificate of registration to the owner of such dog if the owner presents to the code enforcement officer or police officer sufficient evidence of:
(1) A proper enclosure to confine the dangerous dog; and
(2) The posting of the premises where the dangerous dog is located with a clearly visible sign warning that there is a dangerous dog present (such sign shall prominently display the dangerous dog symbol designed by the Georgia Department of Natural Resources).
(c) In addition to the requirements of subsection (b) of this section, the owner of a dangerous dog shall present to the governing authority, or its designee, evidence of:
(1) A policy of insurance in the minimum amount of $50,000.00 issued by an insurer authorized to transact business in this state insuring the owner of the dangerous dog against liability for any personal injuries inflicted by the dangerous dog; or
(2) A security bond in the amount of $50,000.00 or more issued by a surely company authorized to transact business in this state payable to any person or persons injured by the dangerous dog.
(d) The owner of a dangerous dog shall notify the governing authority within 24 hours if the dog is on the loose, is confined, has attacked a human, has died or has been sold, donated, or disposed of, and if the dog has been sold, donated or disposed of, the owner shall provide the governing authority, or its designee, with the name, address, email address and telephone number of the new owner of the dog.
(e) The owner of the dangerous dog shall notify the governing authority, or its designee, if the owner is moving from the unincorporated area of the county, and the owner of a dangerous dog who is a new resident of the unincorporated area of the county shall register the dog as required in this section within 30 days after becoming a resident.
(f) Issuance of a certificate of registration or the renewal of a certificate of registration by the governing authority, or its designee, does not warrant or guarantee that the requirements specified in subsection (b) and (c) of this section were met or are maintained by the owner of a dangerous dog.
(g) An animal control officer is authorized to make whatever inquiry is deemed necessary to ensure compliance with the provisions of this article.
(Ord. No. 2025-2, § I, 4-7-2025)
242:
It is unlawful for an owner of a dangerous dog to permit the dog to be outside a proper enclosure unless the dog is muzzled and restrained by a proper chain or leash and is under the physical restraint of a responsible person. The muzzle shall be made in a manner that will not cause injury to the dog or interfere with its vision or respiration but will prevent it from biting any person.
(Ord. No. 2025-2, § I, 4-7-2025)
243:
(a) A dangerous dog shall be immediately confiscated by an animal control officer if the:
(1) Owner of such dog does not secure or maintain the liability insurance or bond required by this article;
(2) The dog is not validly registered as required by this article;
(3) The dog is not maintained in the proper enclosure, or
(4) The dog is outside a proper enclosure in violation of this article.
(b) Any dog that has been confiscated under the provisions of this section shall be returned to its owner upon the owner's compliance with provisions of this article and upon the payment of reasonable confiscation costs including the boarding at a rate (current rate as set by governing authority), per day, plus a pickup fee of $50.00 and the current cost of rabies vaccination if the animal's owner does not produce proof of a current rabies vaccination. In the event the owner has not complied with the provisions of this article within the 20 days of the date the dog was confiscated, said dog shall be destroyed in an expeditious and humane manner.
(Ord. No. 2025-2, § I, 4-7-2025)

248:
(a) To obtain a building permit, mobile home location/relocation permit or a certificate of occupancy, an applicant must apply at the county tax assessor's office.
(b) Requirements.
(1) A 911 address must be obtained. The 911 address can be obtained from the emergency services center.
(2) An on-site septic tank inspection must be obtained from the health department and/or old existing septic tanks must be re-inspected by the health department.
(3) The applicant must present proof of current year paid taxes on mobile home.
(4) The applicant must obtain location/relocation permit from the tax assessor's office. The fee for the permit shall be in an amount as established by the board of commissioners from time to time and includes a 911 sign and post. The applicant's address must also be displayed before calling code enforcement.
a. Once the permit is acquired, only a hauler and installer registered and licensed with the state can locate and set up a manufactured home, modular home or mobile home within the county.
b. Before a mobile home can be relocated, the current year tax decal and relocation permit must be affixed to the mobile home.
(5) Once installation is complete, the installer must complete the installer certificate and attach the certificate to the inside of the panel box door in the mobile home. When all items on the attached compliance list are complete, the applicant may contact the code enforcement.
(6) Contact code enforcement for inspection to obtain an occupancy permit.
(7) When moving a mobile home out of the county or to a valid mobile home dealership, an exit permit must be purchased from the tax assessor office. applicant must present a receipt from the tax commissioner indicating all the county taxes have been paid. The exit permit shall be in an amount as established by the board of commissioners from time to time.
(c) Compliance inspection checklist.
(1) Street access. Each manufactured home stand or lot shall be provided with access frontage to a width of at least 30 feet to a public or private street or road.
(2) Miscellaneous general standards.
a. Exterior doors will be metal or wood and in working order.
b. Floors will be intact and in good repair.
c. Every window will have glass panes. No other material is acceptable.
d. Siding of all units shall be completely intact and shall not expose any interior material including insulation, wiring, framing or similar material usually found within the exterior of the home.
e. Rust or damage must not be visible on the exterior of the unit.
f. All units have an operable, and in good working order, hot and cold water system, a toilet, kitchen sink, bathroom sink, tub, or shower, electrically certified heating appliance and cooking appliance.
g. There shall be no exposed electrical wiring or exposed plumbing on the interior or exterior of the home. Electrical wiring must be encased in conduit from panel box on the service pole to a depth of 18 inches and all the way to the floor of the home. Water line and sewer line must be connected.
h. Underpinning, skirting and other siding must be in place 15 days after inspection. It must cover the entire home with spaces. Skirting material must be masonry, concrete, stucco, masonite, metal or vinyl. No roofing tin-like material is to be used.
i. Certification from the installer that the mobile home was set up and installed in accordance with the requirements of chapter 120-3-7 of Rules and Regulations for Manufactured Homes or the manufacturer's installation instructions, whichever is appropriate.
j. All manufactured, modular, or mobile homes and all habitable spaces added to the home shall meet the minimum standards or the standards that from time to time are adopted by the county board of commissioners.
(Ord. of 6-1-2009)
251:
(a) No electrical connection permit shall be issued unless and until the applicant (proposed "purchaser") has:
(1) Been issued a valid septic tank permit by the county board of health if a sewage disposal system is required;
(2) Or if the purpose is to reconnect or re-establish electrical service to a site that had previously been provided with electricity, then a certification from the county board of health that any on-site sewage disposal system existing or required by the site complies with health laws and regulations;
(3) Nor shall such a permit be issued until a mobile home site permit has been issued if one is required under the provisions of the mobile home site permit article.
(b) Exemptions.
(1) The provisions of this article shall not apply to those situations where the provider of electrical service is restoring service to a "purchaser" who had previously been disconnected due to nonpayment of utility bills or actions of the elements.
(2) Any property which has been inspected by the county health department sanitation inspector and found to be in compliance with the county health code regulations, shall be exempt from further inspection and from the requirement of obtaining an electrical permit required by this article for a period of five years from the date of said inspection. The county health department shall maintain a list of all inspected properties, with the date of said inspection, and furnish a copy of same to all electrical providers. It shall not be a violation of this article for any electrical provider to provide electrical service to any property which has been so inspected within five years, as no electrical permit shall be required under this article for said property.
(Ord. of 3-6-2000, art. 4)
252:
Should an applicant for an electrical connection permit represent his application for the permit that the electrical service requested on the subject site is to service a self-contained travel trailer or motor home and there will be no on-site disposal of sewage, then the applicant shall not be required to obtain any sewage disposal permit from the county health department prior to the issuance of an electrical connection permit; provided, however, the applicant must enter into a written agreement with the county in a form from time to time prescribed by the county, wherein the applicant acknowledges that the electrical connection permit shall authorize an electrical service for use by the self-contained travel trailer or motor home only, and should the electrical service be used to service any other facility, or should any on-site disposal of sewage occur on the subject site in violation of existing regulations of the county health department, then the electrical connection permit shall be deemed null and void and the "provider" upon the written request of the board shall have authority to terminate, disconnect and remove all electrical service from the subject site.
(Ord. of 3-6-2000, art. 5)
253:
This article shall apply to all unincorporated land located within the boundaries of the county. Authority for electrical permits for property located within the city limits of incorporated towns of Cobbtown, Collins, Glennville, Manassas, and Reidsville shall vest with the city building inspector or other designated city representative.
(Ord. of 1-9-2004, § I(art. 1.2); Ord. of 4-4-2005(1), § I(art. 1.2))
254:
As used in this article, the following terms shall have the following meanings, except where the context clearly indicates a different meaning:
Building means any home or other structure having a roof and intended for shelter, housing or enclosure of persons, animals, or property of any kind, character or description. This includes but is not limited to manufactured, mobile and modular homes.
Electrical connection permit means a permit, issued by the designated county official, who from time to time is designated by the board as the official authorized to issue such permits for the unincorporated area of the county, which permit authorizes a provider of electrical services to furnish electricity to a particular site, structure or purchaser.
Pre-approved locations means all existing buildings or locations with electrical service as of the effective date of the enactment of this article.
Provider of electrical service means any utility company or person, firm, corporation, partnership, or other legal entity which sells, furnishes or delivers for sale electrical service within the county.
Purchaser means any person or firm, corporation, partnership, society, club, or association of persons acting together as a unit who purchase or cause to be purchased electrical service within the county.
(Ord. of 1-9-2004, § I(art. 3); Ord. of 4-4-2005(1), § I(art. 3))
255:
(a) New electrical services shall not be provided to any building by a utility company or individual whether by individual electrical meter, or power feeds or drop cords as shared service from another structure, without having applied for and received an approved electrical connection permit from the county.
(b) All existing locations are pre-approved.
(c) Existing locations can be put on an "out of compliance list" if found to be out of compliance with any county ordinance, state law, federal law, or past due on any state or county tax or user fees. After the owner or other person occupying the building has been given notice and 30 days to come into compliance, a list of the locations on the "out of compliance" list shall be provided to all utility providers serving the county.
(d) An "out of compliance" list shall be periodically compiled by the designated county official not less than every quarter. An "out of compliance list" shall be posted at the county commissioners' office and shall be available to any person upon request at the county commissioners' office and a copy shall be provided to all power companies operating within the county.
(e) Once a location has been placed on the "out of compliance list" and service interrupted for any reason an electrical permit must be acquired before service can be reinstated.
(f) Existing locations not on the "out of compliance list" may be transferred without any new permits or interruptions of services.
(g) In the case of a manufactured, mobile or modular home, a new electrical permit is required any time the home is relocated from a permanent site to another site.
